articles.title: Virat Kohli birthday: 10 inspiring quotes from the batting superstar
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli has inspired people not just with his batting but also with his words.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli has inspired people not just with his batting but also with his words. Over the years, his thoughts on hard work, success, self-belief and handling pressure have motivated many young cricketers.Kohli has won almost every major trophy in cricket. His list of titles includes the 50-over World Cup, the T20 World Cup, two Champions Trophy titles and two Indian Premier League (IPL) trophies.He is also India's most successful Test captain. Under his leadership, India won 40 of 68 Tests and lost 17.A look at Virat Kohli's careerKohli has played 123 Tests for India and scored 9,230 runs at an average of 46.85. He has 30 centuries and 31 half-centuries in the format. He is India's fourth-highest run-scorer in Test cricket.In ODIs, Kohli is the world's second-highest run-scorer. He has scored 15,183 runs in 318 matches at an average of 58.84. His tally includes a record 55 centuries and 80 half-centuries.In T20Is, he has scored 4,188 runs in 125 innings at an average of 48.69. He has one century and 38 half-centuries.Across all three formats, Kohli has scored 28,601 runs in 566 matches. His average is 52.86. He has 86 centuries and 149 half-centuries, with a highest score of 254 not out. He is the second-highest run-scorer in international cricket.As Kohli celebrates his 38th birthday on Thursday, here are some of his best quotes.Virat Kohli's quotesSelf-belief and hard work will always earn you success.Whatever you want to do, do with full passion and work really hard towards it. Don't look anywhere else. There will be a few distractions, but if you can be true to yourself, you will be successful for sure.I never stop working. I never stop trying to improve. That is my mantra.There is no shortcut to success.As a kid, I knew everything about my favourite cricketers. I wanted to know everything there was to know about them. Now, I see kids wanting to know so much about me. It feels good.I love playing under pressure. In fact, if there's no pressure, then I'm not in the perfect zone.I like to be myself, and I don't pretend. For instance, I don't dress up for occasions; I am what I am.I always wanted to be one of the top players in the worldA fit body gives you confidence. And there's nothing more impressive than a great attitude, which you can wear on your sleeve.The bat is not a toy, it’s a weapon. It gives me everything in life.You learn everyday, you try to improve everyday. Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 43 runs over a century! Virat Kohli's unexpected choice for his best ODI innings of all time
articles.summary: Virat Kohli has made an unexpected choice while reflecting on his finest ODI innings, placing a 43-run knock against England in the 2013 ICC Champions
articles.body: Virat Kohli has made an unexpected choice while reflecting on his finest ODI innings, placing a 43-run knock against England in the 2013 ICC Champions Trophy final above several of his more celebrated centuries in the format.The former India captain, who turned 38 on Thursday, was featured in a video shared by Star Sports in which he was asked to pick his greatest ODI innings. The interaction came a day after he produced an impressive 74 off just 51 balls against New Zealand.Kohli's selections threw up a few surprises, with the batting great repeatedly favouring innings that might not immediately come to mind when recalling his most memorable performances.His first choice was his 35-run contribution in the 2011 ODI World Cup final against Sri Lanka. He preferred that knock over his unbeaten 133 against Sri Lanka in Hobart in 2012, when India chased down a target of 321 in just 40 overs. He also overlooked his 85 against Australia in the 2023 World Cup opener, an innings played when India were struggling at 2/3 while chasing 199.Kohli continued to back his World Cup final contribution when it was put up against his 122-run effort against England in 2017. That century came during a challenging chase of 351, with India reduced to 63/4. His unbeaten 160 against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018, where he scored 100 runs through running between the wickets, also failed to make the cut.However, when asked to choose between his 35 in the 2011 World Cup final and his performance in the 2013 Champions Trophy final against England, Kohli eventually picked the latter.The 43-run innings came in a rain-affected contest reduced to 20 overs, with India in trouble at 66/5. Kohli joined forces with Ravindra Jadeja to put together a valuable 47-run partnership, while Jadeja contributed an important 33. India eventually clinched the title with a five-run victory.Kohli's final selection also came at the expense of some outstanding centuries. These included his 183 against Pakistan in the 2012 Asia Cup while chasing 330, his 138 against South Africa in Chennai in 2015 and his 107 against Pakistan in the 2015 ODI World Cup. The latter was particularly significant as it made him the first Indian batter to score a World Cup century against Pakistan.Virat Kohli's remarkable international careerKohli has built an extraordinary collection of achievements during his international career. His trophy cabinet includes an ODI World Cup, a T20 World Cup, two Champions Trophy titles and two Indian Premier League (IPL) trophies. He also holds the distinction of being India's most successful Test captain, having guided the team to 40 victories in 68 matches, with 17 defeats.In Test cricket, Kohli has accumulated 9,230 runs in 123 matches at an average of 46.85. His tally includes 30 centuries and 31 half-centuries, making him India's fourth-highest run-scorer in the format.His numbers in ODIs are equally remarkable. Kohli is the second-highest run-getter in the history of the format, with 15,183 runs from 318 matches and 306 innings at an average of 58.84. He has registered 55 centuries, a record in ODI cricket, along with 80 fifties.In T20 Internationals, he has scored 4,188 runs in 125 innings at an average of 48.69, including one century and 38 half-centuries. He ranks third on the all-time run-scoring list in the format.Across all three formats, Kohli has amassed 28,601 international runs in 566 matches and 633 innings at an average of 52.86. His overall tally comprises 86 centuries and 149 half-centuries, with his highest individual score being an unbeaten 254.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Virat Kohli's birthday wishlist: Records that the India talisman would aim to achieve before retiring
articles.summary: From reaching 100 centuries and an elusive ODI double hundred to targeting Rohit's 264, explore the records Virat Kohli could chase before retiring.
articles.body:
India ace Virat Kohli turns 38 with 86 international hundreds, needing 14 more to reach Sachin Tendulkar's 100.

A 60-plus ODI average, a double century and 18,000 runs sit on his list too.

World Cup glory in 2027 and 10,000 IPL runs could cap a remarkable career.

From Rohit Sharma's 264 to Sachin Tendulkar's 100 tons: Virat Kohli's ultimate bucket list on 38th birthday

Virat Kohli has collected almost every honour a batter could ask for, but a birthday is a good occasion to look at the things that are still missing from the collection. The India talisman turned 38 on November 5, and a handful of records and ambitions remain firmly within sight, even if some of them look awfully steep.

Some of these goals are matters of pure arithmetic, such as the hundreds he still needs or the runs required to catch Sachin Tendulkar's ODI total. Others are more personal, including a double century that has always escaped him and a World Cup trophy that slipped away in 2023.

Since he has already stepped away from Tests and T20Is, the 50-over game is now the main stage on which most of this business will be settled. That puts a premium on every series he plays, and every innings carries a little more significance than it once did.

What follows is a wishlist of eight items, taken in roughly the order of their difficulty, starting with the biggest mountain in the sport.

Kohli's 100 international centuries: 14 more needed to match Sachin Tendulkar's record

Kohli currently has 86 international centuries, made up of 55 in ODIs, 30 in Tests and one in T20Is. Tendulkar finished with 100, composed of 51 Test hundreds and 49 in ODIs, so Kohli needs 14 more to join him.

That total is widely regarded as the largest statistical peak in cricket, and it is the item that overshadows the rest of the list. Reaching it would demand a steady run of big scores in a limited number of matches, which is why it remains a long shot even for a batter of his class.

Can Kohli retire with a 60-plus ODI batting average?

His ODI average sits at roughly 58.5 to 59.1 across more than 315 matches, which is already outstanding by any standard. The next step would be to bring it above 60.00 before he calls time.

No batter in history has kept a 60-plus average over a career of 300 or more games, and the players with higher figures than Kohli have all appeared in far fewer matches, somewhere between 50 and 100. A late surge with plenty of not-outs, however, could seal a record that would remain unbeaten for a long time.

Kohli's chase for 18,000 ODI runs and Tendulkar's all-time total

Kohli has scored more than 15,100 ODI runs, which places him second on the all-time list and well ahead of Kumar Sangakkara's 14,234. Tendulkar remains on top with 18,426, a gap of more than 3,300 runs.

Crossing 18,000, or even overtaking Tendulkar, is unlikely, yet it is not out of the question if he continues playing the 50-over format beyond the 2027 World Cup.

Kohli's highest ODI score is the 183 he made against Pakistan in Mirpur in 2012, off 148 balls. He has seven double hundreds in Tests, but no 200 in the 50-over game, which makes it one of the few gaps in his limited-overs record.

There is also a friendly rivalry attached to the target. Rohit Sharma owns three ODI double centuries, including the world-record 264 against Sri Lanka in Kolkata in 2014, and Kohli has never really threatened that mark in a single innings.

Most runs in ODI run chases: Kohli's push towards 9,000

Run chases have always been Kohli's specialty, and the numbers back it up. He has scored over 8,741 runs while batting second, at an average above 66, and he overtook Tendulkar's record of 8,720 in Auckland to become the leading run-scorer in successful and unsuccessful pursuits.

The next landmark is 9,000, which no one has reached in chases before, and at his current pace it looks entirely realistic.

Kohli's 2027 World Cup dream on African soil

Kohli won the ICC World Cup in 2011 as a youngster and finished as runner-up in 2023, so lifting it as a senior player would be the perfect way to bookend a career.

The 2027 tournament will be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, and it is widely expected to be the stage on which his ODI story reaches its final chapter.

Can Kohli become the first batter to score 10,000 IPL runs?

In the IPL, Kohli leads the all-time run charts with more than 9,300 runs. Another 700 or so would make him the first cricketer to cross the 10,000 mark in the tournament's history, a feat that seems well within his grasp over the next season or two.

Why Virat Kohli's wishlist matters more for India than for his own record book

Kohli's list looks like a set of statistical targets, yet the most interesting thing about it is how few of them he actually needs. A man with 86 international centuries, a second-place spot on the all-time ODI run charts and an IPL record that nobody else can possibly match has nothing left to prove, and that freedom may be his biggest asset heading into the next phase of his career.

The hundred international tons is the headline item, and it will draw the most attention, but it is difficult. Fourteen more centuries from a 38-year-old who now plays one format for India is a very tall order, and it would be unfair to judge his remaining years by whether he gets there.

The 2027 World Cup is a far better yardstick. He has won the trophy as a young man and lost the final as a senior one, so a second title in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia would complete a story that his numbers alone cannot tell.

Meanwhile, a run-chase total of 9,000, 10,000 IPL runs and a 60-plus ODI average all reward the very qualities that made him great, namely patience, fitness and an unmatched feel for a target.

Kohli has never needed a list to stay motivated, but for fans, a birthday is the right time to enjoy what is still ahead of him.

articles.title: ‘He got greedy’: Ex-India captain's blunt take on Arshdeep Singh after four-wicket haul
articles.summary: Former India cricketer Ajay Jadeja has praised Arshdeep Singh's overall performance in India's five-wicket victory over New Zealand in the first ODI in
articles.body: Former India cricketer Ajay Jadeja has praised Arshdeep Singh's overall performance in India's five-wicket victory over New Zealand in the first ODI in Auckland, but believes the left-arm pacer could have avoided an expensive finish to his spell.India began their five-match ODI series with a comfortable win at Eden Park on Wednesday, November 4. In a rain-interrupted contest reduced to 32 overs per side, New Zealand were bowled out for 185 before India chased down the revised target of 143 in just 22.4 overs.Virat Kohli led the chase with a fluent 74, while Shubman Gill contributed 37 as the duo stitched together a 113-run partnership. India eventually crossed the finish line with five wickets to spare and 56 deliveries remaining.With the ball, Arshdeep was India's leading wicket-taker, claiming four wickets in his 10 overs. However, his figures of 4/70 were inflated by an expensive final over in which New Zealand tailender Blair Tickner struck him for three sixes, taking 23 runs off the over.Assessing the pacer's performance, Jadeja felt Arshdeep had been impressive for most of his spell but allowed the opportunity to complete a five-wicket haul to influence his bowling towards the end."I would call him slightly greedy. He himself said that as well. If you remove his last over, he had dismissed four batters before that and had given 40-odd runs. He got slightly greedy for the fifth wicket in the last over," Jadeja said on Sony Sports Network.Arshdeep had himself admitted after the match that the fifth wicket would have been his favourite, indicating that he was keen to complete a five-wicket haul. Despite missing out on the milestone, his four-wicket effort placed him in an exclusive group of Indian fast bowlers to achieve the feat in an ODI in New Zealand, alongside Javagal Srinath and Mohammed Shami.Jadeja, however, stressed that the expensive final over should not overshadow what Arshdeep brings to India's bowling combination. He pointed to the value of having a left-arm fast bowler in an attack that already features Jasprit Bumrah, adding that the competition for places would only benefit the team."It happens. It's natural, but Arshdeep Singh is showing that he can play in ODIs as well, which I believe is a very good thing when a left-arm seamer gets added to this attack with (Jasprit) Bumrah. The competition has increased a lot, which is very good for India," Jadeja elaborated.Jadeja impressed with Anshul KambojJadeja also reserved praise for Anshul Kamboj, who delivered an economical spell of 2/22 from his 10 overs and walked away with the Player of the Match award.The former India batter acknowledged that Kamboj had faced questions over his bowling during his Test debut against England in 2025, particularly regarding his pace and tendency to bowl no-balls. However, he felt the youngster had shown considerable improvement in Auckland.Jadeja also suggested that Kamboj's workload before the England assignment could have contributed to his struggles, pointing out that fatigue can affect a bowler's execution. His performance against New Zealand, according to Jadeja, reflected better pace, consistency and accuracy."He bowled extremely well. The vision everyone had was that he didn't have pace when he played in England and was bowling a lot of no-balls. I think he had come after playing a lot of cricket then. So a guy also gets tired. It's not that easy. Then he was playing for the first time, but the consistency and the slight increase in his pace he showed today (Wednesday), if we talk about the accuracy amongst the four bowlers, it's Anshul Kamboj," Jadeja added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Chennai Super Kings (CSK) and Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) have agreed to a four-player trade ahead of the IPL 2027 season, with both franchises making significant changes to their squads.Under the deal, England all-rounder Liam Livingstone and Australian seam-bowling all-rounder Jack Edwards will move to CSK, while left-arm pacer Khaleel Ahmed and Australian fast bowler Nathan Ellis will join SRH.Livingstone has been transferred to CSK for INR 6 crore, taking a substantial pay cut from the INR 13 crore at which SRH had originally acquired him.Edwards, meanwhile, will join the Chennai-based franchise at his existing fee of INR 3 crore. SRH had signed the Australian all-rounder before his international debut, but he did not get an opportunity to feature in IPL 2026 after a foot injury ruled him out of the entire season.In exchange, SRH will secure the services of Khaleel at his existing contract value of INR 4.8 crore. The left-arm pacer is familiar with the Hyderabad franchise, having represented them between 2018 and 2021.Khaleel moved to CSK ahead of IPL 2025 and made an impact with 15 wickets in 14 matches. However, his IPL 2026 campaign was cut short after he suffered a right quadriceps injury. He managed to play only five matches during the season before being ruled out.The fourth player involved in the exchange is Nathan Ellis, who will move to SRH at his existing fee of INR 2 crore. The Australian quick, known for his variations and ability to deliver in the death overs, brings considerable T20 experience to Hyderabad's pace attack.Ellis was also unavailable throughout IPL 2026 after suffering a severe hamstring injury that forced him to miss the entire tournament.The four-player exchange gives CSK two overseas all-rounders in Livingstone and Edwards, while SRH strengthen their bowling resources with the additions of Khaleel and Ellis ahead of the 2027 campaign.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Selectors could be forced to think’: Irfan Pathan backs Anshul Kamboj for 2027 ODI World Cup
articles.summary: Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan believes Anshul Kamboj has the potential to become a contender for India's 2027 ODI World Cup squad, suggesting that
articles.body: Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan believes Anshul Kamboj has the potential to become a contender for India's 2027 ODI World Cup squad, suggesting that consistent performances could make it difficult for the selectors to overlook the young fast bowler.Kamboj impressed with the ball in India's five-wicket victory over New Zealand in the rain-affected first ODI at Auckland on Wednesday. Making good use of the seaming conditions, the Chennai Super Kings (CSK) pacer returned figures of 2/22 from his 10 overs, sending down an impressive 46 dot balls.His disciplined effort played an important role in restricting New Zealand to 185. Arshdeep Singh led the attack with four wickets, while Gurnoor Brar picked up three as India bundled out the hosts.India subsequently chased down the revised target of 143 in 22.4 overs, with Virat Kohli leading the way through an authoritative 74 off 51 deliveries.Speaking in a video by Cricinfo, Pathan backed Kamboj to make further progress, pointing out that his difficult introduction to international cricket should be viewed in the context of the circumstances surrounding his debut.The former all-rounder felt Kamboj had not been given sufficient recovery time after travelling before being pushed into Test cricket. The fast bowler made his Test debut last year as an injury replacement but endured a difficult outing, managing just one wicket while conceding 89 runs in 18 overs at an economy rate of nearly five.Pathan stressed that adjusting to different conditions, recovering from travel and preparing for the demands of Test cricket can take time for a fast bowler."He will be one of the bowlers for sure. What happened during the Test match, we have to understand. It is not easy to play a Test match after travelling. For any bowler to get adjusted to the climate, recovery and then go from there, it takes time. Anshul that time, needed more time to play Test cricket," he said.Pathan also highlighted Kamboj's versatility, particularly his ability to contribute with both the new and old ball. He pointed to the pacer's death-bowling skills, including his ability to deliver wide yorkers from around the wicket, which he has demonstrated while representing CSK.According to Pathan, having multiple skills at his disposal makes Kamboj a valuable option for the future. He also backed the youngster to climb the ranks if he continues delivering performances like the one against New Zealand."What I like about him that he can bowl with the new ball and has some good death bowling skill as seen with CSK. He can come round the wicket and bowl the wide yorkers. He bowled with the old ball in this match (against NZ in 1st ODI). He has that package, with the old ball, new ball and can nibble the ball too. He will go up the ladder as far as future is concerned. You would not be surprised if he keeps going like this, selectors would be forced to think about him as one of the WC probables. He is definitely one of them," he added.Kamboj's performance in Auckland comes after a challenging start to his international career, with his domestic and IPL performances having raised expectations before his India debut.His first ODI appearance against the West Indies at New Chandigarh was particularly difficult. The pacer conceded 82 runs in nine overs, with West Indies captain Shai Hope doing much of the damage. Hope scored 42 runs off 31 deliveries against Kamboj, including six fours.However, the disciplined showing against New Zealand offered a reminder of his bowling capabilities. With the ability to operate across different phases of an innings, Kamboj has now given himself an opportunity to strengthen his case for a longer run in India's ODI setup, with the 2027 World Cup on the horizon. articles.title: Gloucestershire to rebrand to Bristol in T20 Blast from 2027
articles.summary: Gloucestershire will compete under the name of Bristol in the T20 Blast from next season in a big to attract new audiences and address falling revenue.
articles.body:
Gloucestershire will no longer compete in the T20 Blast under the county's name, instead rebranding to Bristol from 2027.

The club have played all formats of the county game since 1870 as Gloucestershire but are taking the strategic decision to change identity in a bid to "reach a new audience" to address falling ticket revenue and heralded it as 'an exciting new chapter.'

The club revealed their intentions in a club strategy meeting for members in the Grace Room in the pavilion at Bristol's Seat Unique Stadium on Wednesday night, with another meeting set for Thursday evening in Cheltenham to discuss the plans.

Neil Priscott, the club's chief executive officer, and Jenny Hall, head of audience development, informed members of the club's strategic direction and future plans, with members of the club board also in attendance.

Priscott told members they plan to "invest in Gloucestershire's future – strengthening our club identity as we pursue our top-eight ambition, while creating a distinct Bristol-based T20 team to reach a new audience."

While overall attendances are increasing, the Blast - which drives 20% of the club's ticketing revenue - is declining.

A statement by the club on Thursday said players, members, key stakeholders and the ECB had been consulted over several months in order to "shape an exciting new chapter in our evolution".

It added: "Building on more than 150 years of proud heritage, Gloucestershire Cricket will always remain our overarching identity and the foundation of everything we do.

"As part of our wider strategic vision to grow domestic cricket, attract new audiences across the region, and drive commercial reinvestment back into the sport, we will be creating a new dedicated T20 identity for our men's and women's teams."

Fixtures for the 2027 Blast will be released on 24 November with Gloucestershire's new name, kit and logo expected to be released at the same time.

The club won the Blast for the only time in 2024, thrashing West Country rivals Somerset at Edgbaston to pick up their first silverware in nine years, but revenue from the competition was down 21% in 2026 compared to 2025.

Warwickshire rebranded to the Birmingham Bears in 2014 , and saw an increase in commercial income with then-Warwickshire CEO Colin Povey saying at the time: "We've got to get more people through the gates and attract a new audience."

The decision was reversed 12 years later, with the Bears returning under the Warwickshire banner this past season and current CEO Stuart Cain said: "The club decided to be bold with a city-based name for our T20 team, and it saw attendances grow to record levels and attract new fans to the Bears.

"But with our long-term future in mind, and following feedback from members, now is the right time for change.

"We represent the county, and that's what returning to Warwickshire Bears is about."

'Marketing madness - people will feel detached from the club'

Gloucestershire life member Tim Lezard, who has been watching the club play for 40 years and wrote the book Never Say Die, celebrating the club's One-Day Cup win in 2015 said he was horrified when he heard the news on Wednesday evening.

Lezard told BBC Radio Gloucestershire: "We have been playing in Gloucestershire for 156 years, we have played across the county - it's hugely important to the club.

"We were told that the history and heritage is really important during this glossy presentation [only] to then go and try and totally wipe it out in one move of marketing madness.

"Everyone I have spoken to is appalled by it. There are no positive comments whatsoever. Some people are saying they just wouldn't bother going to watch if the name changes."

Lezard said he understood the club's reasons for trying to attract additional income but called the decision "a massive misstep".

"Nobody is crying out for the name to be changed," he said. "I am sure the club are trying to do the right thing by trying to attract new people, but they are also taking people for fools – do people really not understand that Gloucestershire play in Bristol.

"What they are doing is alienating all those people in the north of the county who will feel this complete detachment from this new club.

"I think they've gone down the wrong path, I understand the reasons. I applaud the club for trying to do something positive and encourage people to come and watch, we all need that, but to just get rid of 156 years of history is a massive misstep I think.

"I think it will be a interesting meeting [in Cheltenham], maybe quite feisty, I think there will be a lot of opposition to it.

"I think they're playing with fire, I can't see how people are going to support this name change."

articles.body: The opening ODI of India's upcoming home series against Sri Lanka has been shifted from Delhi to Visakhapatnam, with the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) confirming the venue change on Thursday. The December 13 fixture, originally scheduled to be played at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, will now take place at the ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium in Visakhapatnam.Why has India vs Sri Lanka 1st ODI been shifted?The DDCA had approached the BCCI seeking a change in venue, citing its inability to host the international fixture amid renovation work and unfavourable weather conditions expected in Delhi during December.The association was concerned that the ongoing work at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, coupled with the possibility of weather-related disruptions, could affect the smooth organisation of the match. The BCCI subsequently approved the request and confirmed Visakhapatnam as the new venue for the series opener.India vs Sri Lanka: Revised ODI and T20I scheduleSri Lanka are scheduled to play three ODIs and three T20Is during their tour of India in December 2026. articles.title: If Virat Kohli wants to play Vijay Hazare Trophy, I would love to have him: Vijay Dahiya
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi coach Vijay Dahiya said he would love to have Virat Kohli in the dressing room if the senior India batter wants to play the Vijay Hazare
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi coach Vijay Dahiya said he would love to have Virat Kohli in the dressing room if the senior India batter wants to play the Vijay Hazare Trophy, which is scheduled to begin on December 14."If he wants to play, I would love to have him in this dressing room. I would love to have him there just to talk to the boys. I won't let him go home. I'll make him sit in the dressing room and tell the boys about his journey, the hard work, the ethics and the honour of playing for the country," Dahiya told reporters at the Air Force Complex Ground in Palam."I have seen him through all the stages. I can tell the boys where he started and where he is today. There is a pathway. Maybe you cannot become Virat, but you can become someone if you do certain things the right way."The Ranji Trophy match between Delhi and Services ended in a draw, with Delhi walking away with three points after taking the first-innings lead.Kohli played two matches for Delhi in the Vijay Hazare Trophy last season, scoring 131 and 77 against Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat, respectively.Kohli, who turned 38 on Thursday and now plays only one format, is set to feature in India's three-match ODI series against Sri Lanka on December 13, 16 and 19. He will miss Delhi's first three Vijay Hazare Trophy matches against Goa, Punjab and Rajasthan but could join the team for its December 21 clash against Chandigarh.Dahiya, who has witnessed Kohli's growth since his junior days, also narrated an interaction with Delhi opener Priyansh Arya after the latter was dismissed on Day 4 of the Ranji Trophy fixture against Services.Delhi were set a target of 320 runs in 56 overs, with Arya caught at deep square leg off Jayant Goyat's bowling."He asked me, 'If Virat was there, how would he have chased this total?' We worked it out and discussed how he would have approached the chase," Dahiya said."That's the reason why I said I would love to have him there. He was there last season as well. I would love to have him there just to talk to the boys."I won't let him go home. I will make him sit in the dressing room and tell the boys, step by step, about his journey."I have seen him through all the stages. I can tell them where he was and where he is today. There is a pathway. Maybe you cannot become Virat, but you can become someone if you do certain things the right way," Dahiya said.Dahiya also expressed his desire to have veteran India pacer Ishant Sharma, who has played 105 Tests, as a mentor for Delhi's red-ball team."Somebody who has played 100 Test matches can come back. He should be here as a mentor for red-ball cricket and share his ideas," he said.Dahiya said Ishant was working hard and remained available for white-ball cricket."He is working hard right now. I asked him, and he said he was bowling really well. So he is definitely available as far as white-ball cricket is concerned," Dahiya said, referring to Ishant's availability for the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy and Vijay Hazare Trophy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'What I have learnt is that I should not think so much ahead': Prithvi Shaw prefers to stay in the present
articles.summary: KOLKATA: Prithvi Shaw showed glimpses of his vintage best as he led Maharashtra to a 10-wicket victory against Bengal in the Ranji Trophy Elite Group ‘C’
articles.body: KOLKATA: Prithvi Shaw showed glimpses of his vintage best as he led Maharashtra to a 10-wicket victory against Bengal in the Ranji Trophy Elite Group ‘C’ match at the Eden Gardens here on Thursday. The opener got his second half-century in this Ranji season to stay unbeaten on 53 off 50 balls while striking three fours and four sixes during his innings.However, Shaw preferred not to look too far ahead but stay in the present. “What I have learnt from experience is that I should not think so much ahead,” he said.“Like I am giving an interview now. After this, I will go to the room and then think about what to do. I don’t think more than that. Just keep winning games. Have good training. Eat well,” he said, laying down his programme.The 26-year-old last played for India five years ago and would definitely look to make a return to the national side. “There is always that thought at the back of the mind. But now I do not think so much ahead,” he explained.His immediate challenge is to put together a consistent run of scores in domestic cricket.The explosive opener has hit two half-centuries in seven innings this Ranji season, with his highest score of 70 coming against Delhi in Maharashtra’s opening match. Since then, he has scored 7, 21, 0, 17 and 12.“Some innings will go bad and some will go well. There is no problem with my start. Big runs are just a matter of one innings,” he felt.Shaw is enjoying leading Maharashtra after shifting from Mumbai last season.“I feel Mumbai and Pune are not too far apart. There is a difference of 1.5 to 2 hours, and I know a lot of players. Ritu (Gaikwad), Ankit (Bawne) here. So I never felt that I have come far from home. I am very comfortable, and have enjoyed it a lot,” he said.The opener enjoyed facing experienced pacer Mohammed Shami. “Shami Bhai is bowling as he used to. There is no change. He is bowling fast. It was about how to play Shami Bhai well because I feel he is the main bowler for such wickets,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From near-draw to 106-run victory: Sarfaraz, Musheer script Mumbai's dramatic Ranji Trophy revival vs Railways
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Sarfaraz Khan didn't have much to do for most of Day Four.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Sarfaraz Khan didn't have much to do for most of Day Four. While batting, he played second fiddle to Divyaansh Sksena, guiding his young teammate to a maiden first-class century. While fielding, he was mostly moving up and down the pitch, taking his position in the slip cordon in anticipation of a moment that would change the course of the match.That moment came in the 67th over when his brother Musheer (3/42) induced a top edge from Eshaan Goyal. Sarfaraz anticipated it well, sprinted to his right from first slip and completed a diving catch to dismiss Goyal, sparking a Mumbai revival. Mumbai soon wrapped up Railways to record a 106-run win in their Elite Group D Ranji Trophy match at the Brabourne Stadium on Thursday.Till that point, the match looked headed for a draw as Goyal (102, 201b; 11x4, 1x6) and Zubair Ali (115, 117b; 14x4, 5x6) thwarted Mumbai's attack, brought up their centuries in contrasting styles and stitched together a 167-run partnership for the sixth wicket to lift Railways from 83/5 to 250/5.Even Mumbai skipper Siddhesh Lad felt the match was heading towards a stalemate, but he added that the team kept believing till which took them over the line."We kept fighting till the last hour. Whenever we were regrouping during the breaks, there was always belief among each one of us that we were just one wicket away. We just wanted to slow things down a bit at that stage (when the partnership was building) so that we could break their momentum. We did that and I'm very happy with how the boys have reacted throughout the four games," Lad said after the match.Sarfaraz's catch turned the match on its head as the 42-time champions seized the opportunity, and 11.1 overs later were celebrating their fourth outright victory on the trot. The win puts them firmly on top of Group D with 27 points as the team now switches its attention to the Syed Mushtaq Ali T20 Trophy.The day began with Sksena (100*, 136b; 8x4, 1x6) bringing up his century before Mumbai declared at 234/4, setting Railways a target of 372. It was an important knock for the 25-year-old opener, who had made starts in previous matches but had been unable to convert them into substantial scores.Mumbai started their victory march in the earnest, kept taking wickets at regular intervals, and had reduced Railways to 83/5. Shams Mulani (4/69) led the charge with three wickets, while Tanush Kotian (2/93) claimed one and another came through a run-out effected by Sarfaraz and Mulani.But Mumbai's players knew that on the Brabourne wicket, once batters got set, it would be difficult to dislodge them. That proved to be the case as Goyal and Zubair dug in during their bid to steer Railways to safety. They batted together for 36.3 overs before Sarfaraz's intervention broke their association.A couple of overs later, Musheer dismissed Zubair, who holed out to Suryansh Shedge at mid-off. Mulani then got Toufik Mondal thanks to a brilliant catch by Kotian at short mid-wicket, shortly after Sarfaraz had sledged the left-hander into playing an attacking shot. Kotian trapped Raj Choudhury lbw before Musheer had last-man Himanshu Sangwan caught at silly point to seal the victory.Skipper Lad was full of praise for Sarfaraz, saying: "Sarfaraz was outstanding. He is a special fielder. He had dropped a catch before that, but he wanted to do something for the team. That is what we saw."While Mumbai are off to a solid start, Lad wants his troopers to be at the top of their game when red-ball cricket returns in January 2027. Mumbai will resume their campaign against Uttarakhand at the Wankhede Stadium."We don't want to be satisfied with what we have done in the first four games because we have a long journey ahead and we want to do something special, add something to the legacy of Mumbai this season. We will have to regroup after the white-ball phase. That's why it was important to win all four games because, in the second half, the momentum might not be with us. We will have to work very hard to get even a single point," Lad said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Bengal suffer season’s first loss, slip to second spot
articles.summary: KOLKATA: Bengal’s unbeaten run in this Ranji season came to a grinding halt as they went down to Maharashtra in an Elite Group ‘C’ match by 10 wickets at
articles.body: KOLKATA: Bengal’s unbeaten run in this Ranji season came to a grinding halt as they went down to Maharashtra in an Elite Group ‘C’ match by 10 wickets at Eden Gardens here on Thursday.Maharashtra recorded their second outright victory and by virtue of gaining the maximum seven points from this win, dislodged Bengal from the top to go into the Ranji break as table-toppers with 19 points.Bengal, returning empty-handed from their second home match of this season, are at second spot with 18 points with Gujarat breathing down their neck with 16 points at third place.Despite losing considerable amount of play to bad light and rain over the last three days, that Maharashtra won this tie with a session of play remaining, speaks poorly of Bengal’s quality of play.Skipper Abhimanyu Easwaran was candid in admitting that. “It’s the way we lost that hurts most,” he said after the match. “We played poor cricket,” he added.His counterpart Prithvi Shaw gave full credit to his boys. “I think our bowlers did both the job for us in the first innings,” he smiled while mentioning the 72-run last-wicket stand between Tanay Sanghavi and Pradeep Dadhe in the first innings. “It was an even match till then, but once we had them (Bengal) four down on Day III, we felt like we could win this match,” he said.Resuming at one run ahead of the Maharashtra score, Bengal were bowled out for 186 in 54.4 overs in their second innings, adding just 110 runs while losing their remaining six wickets in less than 31 overs.After the quick dismissals of Suraj Sindhu Jaiswal and Shahbaz Ahmed, Abishek Porel and Sumanta Gupta then tried to steady the ship by building up a partnership. Porel got his half-century off 68 balls but fell soon after edging one from left-arm spinner Hitesh Walunj that jumped a bit awkwardly to Digvijay Singh at first slip for 65.Pradipta Pramanik fell to a brilliant diving catch by Ankit Bawne at mid-wicket off Hitesh, who also claimed Mohammed Shami’s wicket to finish with four for 53.When Sumanta Gupta dragged one of pacer Dadhe’s delivery on to his stumps in the third over after the lunch break, Maharashtra needed 112 runs to win.Openers Shaw and Sachin Dhas took the side home in just 19.4 overs before the tea break by playing some aggressive cricket.The visitors reached 50 in seven overs with Dhas getting 34 of those runs. However, Shaw joined the party too as he lifted left-arm spinner Shahbaz Ahmed for a six each in his consecutive overs.Shaw stayed unbeaten on 53 off 50 balls, striking three fours and four sixes while Dhas was unconquered on 61 off 68 deliveries, hitting 10 boundaries, as Maharashtra finished with 114 without loss.Brief Scores: Bengal 143 & 186 (Abhishek Porel 65, Sumanta Gupta 59, Ankur Paul 32; Pradeep Dadhe 4-48, Hitesh Walunj 4-53). Maharashtra 218 & 114/0 (Sachin Dhas 61 no, Prithvi Shaw 53 no). Maharashtra won by 10 wickets.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
